name: Samvedi

sources.citation: English Wikipedia, 'Kadodi language' (accessed 2026-09-17 via direct download).
sources.note: Nothing; sociolinguistic summary citing only Ethnologue.

Nothing on stress; gives a few sound correspondences (c > s, initial s > h, -o > -ɔ in verb forms) and names Naresh Naik's book 'सामवेदी बोली - संरचना आणि स्वरूप' (Kalelkar prize 2018) and Paul Rumao's folk-literature collections.

sources.citation: Eberhard, Simons & Fennig (eds.). 2019. Ethnologue, 22nd ed., entry 'Samvedi' (smv), via Internet Archive copy 2019-05-12.
sources.note: Nothing; only 'A divergent dialect of, or closely related language to Konkani [knn]. Shares many features with Gujarati [guj].' Status 6a* Vigorous, Maharashtra.

sources.citation: Naik, Naresh. 2013. Vasai Jilha Thane parisaratil Samvedi bolicha chikitsak abhyas [A critical study of the Samvedi dialect of the Vasai area, Thane District]. PhD thesis, Dept. of Marathi, University of Mumbai (guide H. Thorat), 316 pp., Marathi.
sources.note: The only full-length linguistic description of Samvedi; a 316-page structural study almost certainly has a phonology (dhvani/ucchar) chapter where an aghat (stress) statement would sit. Chapter PDFs are listed on Shodhganga (06_chapter, 23 MB, is the largest and a likely phonology chapter) but the PDF server on port 8443 was could not be reached by automated download and from direct download; retry from another network or via INFLIBNET.

tone.quote: दैनंदिन जीवनातील नैमित्तिक बोलणे, . निवेदन, कथन यातील स्वरस्वनांची ध्वनीपातळी मध्यम (॥0) राहते. संभाषण, संबोधन व प्रश्‍नोत्तरात ही पातळी उच्च (५91) होते.जायूगनी, आढ्‌गनी, ठोवूगनी आशा आज्ञार्थी विधानात अन्त्य स्वरस्वनाची ध्वनीपातळी अतिउच्च (रत -॥5॥) होते. [...] (p. 213:) अवरोही वाक्‍्यसुराने(0) विधान वाक्य सूचित होते तर आरोही वाक्‍्यसुराने (/) प्रश्‍नवाक्य सूचित होते. आरोह हा अंत:स्तरापासूनन आलेला असतो म्हणजे भाषकाच्या सुराने प्रश्‍नवाक्य सूचित होतच असते.
tone.locator: ch. 7 sec. 7:1 'Samvedi bolichya svanavyavasthechi vaishishtye', p. 279; and ch. 5 sec. 5:14, p. 213
tone.translation: In everyday casual speech, narration and story-telling the pitch level of the vowels stays mid; in conversation, address and question-and-answer this level becomes high. In imperative statements such as jayugani, adhgani, thovugani the pitch level of the final vowel becomes extra-high. [...] (p. 213:) A falling sentence-tune signals a declarative sentence, whereas a rising sentence-tune signals a question. The rise comes from the deep structure, i.e. the speaker's tune by itself already signals the question.
tone.check: quotation verified in source (minor differences in wording)

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page for Samvedi (samv1238), listing Grierson 1905 pp. 148-153, Southworth 1976, and Ethnologue 2025 as its only references.
sources.note: Nothing; bibliography only (no descriptive-type reference beyond Grierson).

sources.citation: Grierson, George A. 1905. Linguistic Survey of India, Vol. VII: Indo-Aryan Family, Southern Group: Specimens of the Marathi Language. Calcutta: Office of the Superintendent of Government Printing. Samvedi sketch p. 148, specimen No. 37 pp. 149-153.
sources.note: Nothing. The one-page sketch (p. 148) gives segmental correspondences (ch > s/h, s > h, l > il, genitive/dative endings, verb forms) and calls Samvedi 'a mechanical mixture of Konkan Marathi and Gujarati'; no word on accent, stress or syllable structure. The volume's only accent remarks are in the general notation note (acute accent used when needed) and in the Konkani sections (Karwar/Mangalore Konkani: 'The accent usually rests on the final syllable'), which do not concern Samvedi.
